problem: In a trigonometry test, the class instructor decided that students whose $z$-score is greater than or equal to $-1$ will pass the test. The mean percent score $x$ of the students of the class is $\overset{¯}{x}=64.3%$ with a standard deviation of $\sigma =5.25%.$ Find the minimum passing score.
worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

Substituting $\overset{―}{x}=64.3,$ $z=-1,$ and $\sigma =5.25$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\  & =64.3+(-1)\cdot 5.25 \\  & =64.3-5.25 \\  & =59.05.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the minimum passing score is $59.05%.$
